l4_case_applications.case_name: Sham Wing Kan v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / arrest / search / detention branch landmark pilot
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal declared that section 50(6) PFO authorizes warrantless search of a seized mobile phone's digital contents only in exigent circumstances.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Sham Wing Kan v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / arrest / search / detention branch landmark pilot
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal held that search of digital contents on a phone seized on arrest is governed by the common law power of search incidental to arrest rather than section 50(6) PFO.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Sham Wing Kan v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / arrest / search / detention branch landmark pilot
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal held that any warrantless search of digital phone contents must satisfy the proportionality test.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Sham Wing Kan v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / arrest / search / detention branch landmark pilot
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal applied Keen Lloyd safeguards, emphasizing prior judicial scrutiny for intrusive warrantless digital searches.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / arrest / search / detention branch landmark pilot
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal held that 'specified evidence' under NSL Implementation Rules Schedule 1 covers journalistic material.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / arrest / search / detention branch landmark pilot
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal held that protection for journalistic material in search cases is important but not absolute.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
l4_case_applications.scenario_label: Investigation / arrest / search / detention branch landmark pilot
l4_case_applications.application_summary: The Court of Appeal reasoned that excluding journalistic material from 'specified evidence' would unduly limit effective police investigation in NSL cases.
